title: How many nights do you need on the Nile?
standfirst: Three, four or five nights: here is what each gives you and how to choose. This is part of our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: Three nights
paragraphs: The downstream cruise from Aswan to Luxor. It covers the main temples at a brisk pace and suits a tight schedule.

sections.heading: Four nights
paragraphs: The upstream cruise from Luxor to Aswan, or the classic round of the main sites with a little more time. It is the most popular choice.

sections.heading: Four or five nights on a dahabiya
paragraphs: The dahabiya route from Esna to Aswan, slower and quieter, with smaller sites added. Add a day or two in Luxor beforehand.

sections.heading: Adding time ashore
paragraphs: Many travellers add a night in Aswan or Luxor before or after the cruise, for a site the cruise doesn’t include or simply to rest.

faqs.q: Is a three-night cruise worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, if your time is short. It covers the main sites; a four-night cruise gives more breathing space.

faqs.q: Is a week on the Nile too long?
faqs.a: Week-long cruises are rare. Most people combine a four-night cruise with time in Luxor, Aswan or Cairo.
